video_title: Lakers Sold Again In STUNNING $12.5 Billion Dollar Deal, What Does This Mean For LA?

quotes.speaker: Ramona Shelburne
quotes.summary_phrase: The Lakers have been sold for $12.5 billion
quotes.excerpt: The Lakers being refolded after a little more than a year to a group

text_blocks.speaker: Brian Windhorst
text_blocks.text: The Lakers being refolded after a little more than a year to a group, I assume it will be a group because they will continue to be selling pieces of this is my guess, but to a group with our old boss Bob Iger.

text_blocks.speaker: Tim Bontemps
text_blocks.text: Howdy partners, I'd say you're always on BST, Wendy.

text_blocks.speaker: Ramona Shelburne
text_blocks.text: That was on the T for you, sir.

quotes.speaker: Ramona Shelburne
quotes.summary_phrase: Ramona Shelburne on the Lakers $12.5 billion sale
quotes.excerpt: He just made 2.5 billion in 10 months selling the Lakers.
quotes.quote: I had to take a minute too, Brian, when I first started getting wind of it, very late last night in Los Angeles. I couldn't even really wrap my head around this. Is this right? But you have to run those things down. We all get tips like that and you run them down. I went to bed thinking I was probably right but I wasn't sure yet and then I woke up very early and I knew I was right and then we had to get enough confirmations to go with it. But he owned the team for less than a year, 10 months. It's just, I understand the business aspect. Let's go back to when Mark Walter first became a public figure to us when he bought the Dodgers and that purchase was for 2.15 billion and everybody was like, whoa, that's so much money, right? He just made 2.5 billion in 10 months selling the Lakers. And I don't think that was the initial intention of buying the shares of the Lakers. I think there was grand plans with the Walter Group and the Dodgers and the Lakers. I don't even think he was offering this up. The way this came together is that Josh Kushner and Bob Iger were one of the big groups in Las Vegas and they've been trying to get an expansion team in Vegas. From what I understand, the bidding on that franchise has gotten close to that 10 billion number, at least where they were in that moment was around 10, and that's the same price Mark paid Jeanie Buss when he bought her shares of the Lakers.

quotes.speaker: Ramona Shelburne
quotes.summary_phrase: Mark Walter under investigation by the Department of Justice
quotes.excerpt: There's been some reports over the last few months that Mark's under investigation with the Department of Justice.
quotes.quote: There's been some reports over the last few months that Mark's under investigation with the Department of Justice. Everyone involved denies, blanket denial that this had anything to do with it, but you and I are smart, and Tim, you're also here. I mean, I couldn't resist. That made my summer. I know, I know, I know. I couldn't, you left one on the tee and I didn't swing, so I had to do this one.

quotes.speaker: Tim Bontemps
quotes.summary_phrase: Tim Bontemps on the Lakers' record-breaking sale price
quotes.excerpt: This broke the record that Mark Walter set less than a year ago.
quotes.quote: You don't buy the Lakers to flip them. It's not like a house you buy into a quick remodeling and flip. This is the freaking Los Angeles Lakers and it's just crazy. You see the top two purchase prices of professional sports franchises. This broke the record that Mark Walter set less than a year ago. And it's just a, and look, I get a 25% profit by 2.5 billion dollars. That's more than Tilman Fertitta paid for the Rockets not that long ago.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Brian Windhorst on Mark Walter's SEC investigation
quotes.excerpt: We know that Mark Walter is under investigation by the SEC.
quotes.quote: We know that Mark Walter is under investigation by the SEC. We are not insurance law specialists. We are not assistant US District Attorneys. We are not investigators. But he is under investigation. We know this because there is a suspicion that he might have put too much of his insurance company's money into his other businesses, which are referred to as affiliated companies. Essentially, it's, you know, you're allowed to take some money out of your left pocket and put it into your right, but there's regulation on insurance companies and there's suspicion that maybe not all of the rules were followed.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Brian Windhorst on Mark Walter's purchase of the Lakers
quotes.excerpt: He was a stepped process where he and his partners bought 27% of the Lakers in 2021.
quotes.quote: He was a stepped process where he and his partners bought 27% of the Lakers in 2021 and they gave Jeanie Buss a five-year transition window to remain as the governor, where after that they would do that. You don't do that if you're planning on flipping it.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Brian Windhorst on the Lakers' ownership structure
quotes.excerpt: He owned 27% and now they own Ramona about 77%, is that correct?
quotes.quote: He owned 27% and now they own Ramona about 77%, is that correct? That the Buss family owns 17 or 18 and Patrick Soon-Shiong owns about 7%. We don't know unless you do, how much a percentage are selling. I believe they're buying all of Mark's shares. It's not, he didn't actually make two billion because he didn't pay 10 billion for the team. But I'm not going to get into all that, it has to do with valuations. There's potentially reasons why he would want to get liquidity for his businesses. Again, this is not a financial podcast. And there's also reasons why he would want to potentially be able to show the SEC that he made an investment that returned a big profit for his insurance business.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Brian Windhorst on Josh Kushner's ownership stakes
quotes.excerpt: Josh Kushner is a minority owner of the Miami Heat and previously was a minority owner.
quotes.quote: Josh Kushner is a minority owner of the Miami Heat and previously was a minority owner of the Memphis Grizzlies and therefore has been approved to have that by the NBA. He has been vetted on some level by the NBA and approved by the NBA to own pieces of two different teams. In fact, he will have to sell his share of the Miami Heat, which by the way, the Heat don't sell shares very often. That's a very closely held team. That's neither here nor there.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Brian Windhorst on Bob Iger's relationship with the NBA
quotes.excerpt: Bob Iger has been a long, long time business associate with the NBA and its owners.
quotes.quote: Bob Iger has been a long, long time business associate with the NBA and its owners and top officials. As the CEO of Disney, he was part of the negotiations that have renewed multiple times to be the rights, this is our company, at ESPN. We carry the NBA. Bob Iger has sat at negotiating tables with Adam Silver for years. There's obviously a relationship there.

quotes.speaker: Ramona Shelburne
quotes.summary_phrase: Ramona Shelburne on the Lakers' ownership situation
quotes.excerpt: These are very well-connected guys and they're very bright.
quotes.quote: These are very well-connected guys and they're very bright and that everybody in the league has been talking about what's going on with Mark Walter for the past month or so. I think there's been a Bloomberg story and a Wall Street Journal story. I've been digging on it, I think that's partially how I found out about this is, you know, you're just kind of digging into things and calling the kinds of people who help you understand things like this. And so, they're smart enough to know that what's in the background matters.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Brian Windhorst on Mark Walter's business moves
quotes.excerpt: In the last couple of weeks since this investigation went public, that Mark Walter has been looking.
quotes.quote: In the last couple of weeks since this investigation went public, that Mark Walter has been looking to take businesses that he moved his insurance money into and unwind them so that he can get the money that he gave from his insurance company out of them. I do not want to make an assumption as to why he's doing that, but he's been reportedly investigated for maybe not 100% following all the laws putting his money into affiliated companies and now he's trying to take money out of the affiliated companies and put them back to insurance.

quotes.speaker: Ramona Shelburne
quotes.summary_phrase: Ramona Shelburne on Jeanie Buss's ownership of the Lakers
quotes.excerpt: I have not reported that that was something that Iger said to Kobe.
quotes.quote: I have not reported that that was something that Iger said to Kobe. And I have not confirmed that. Iger's quote left there was definitely a hedge in that quote, you know, great respect for Jeanie, I think, and it was, Jeanie and the family and we're going to do everything we can to honor the agreement that Mark had with her, but things could change, you know, there was a there was a hedge in that quote.

quotes.speaker: Ramona Shelburne
quotes.summary_phrase: Ramona Shelburne on the Lakers' business operations
quotes.excerpt: For now, this is business as usual with the Lakers.
quotes.quote: For now, this is business as usual with the Lakers. They've hired all these new people, they just, you know, completely redid the team. Luka Doncic is looking up going, wow, I thought it was strange in Dallas.

quotes.speaker: Ramona Shelburne
quotes.summary_phrase: Ramona Shelburne on the timeline of the Lakers' sale
quotes.excerpt: The first investigation seems to have started in September of last year.
quotes.quote: The first investigation seems to have started in September of last year. The sale to Mark Walter is approved in October. So, did the NBA, were they fully apprised of what was going on behind the scenes when they approved this sale? I don't know that answer, that's something we all have to go look into and find out. But from what I understand, it was a fairly quick closing. I mean, he just wired six billion dollars. Like he just had it and he wired it.

quotes.speaker: Ramona Shelburne
quotes.summary_phrase: Ramona Shelburne on Chris Paul's relationship with Bob Iger
quotes.excerpt: Chris Paul is a very good friend of Bob Iger's.
quotes.quote: Chris Paul is a very good friend of Bob Iger's. He just recently retired, so he's available. I know he has some production company designs that he's done. I think he's got the world as his oyster, he can do whatever he wants, but if I'm Bob Iger, I think one of my first calls is to Chris Paul and asking how he would like to be involved, if he would like to be involved, etc. But I certainly think that's a name to watch as we go forward here.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Brian Windhorst on the NBA bubble
quotes.excerpt: The NBA bubble was basically put together by Chris Paul and Bob Iger going on walks.
quotes.quote: The NBA bubble was basically put together by Chris Paul and Bob Iger going on walks in the Hollywood Hills during COVID. They put it together. They talk about a partnership, you know, they would put Adam Silver while they were walking and talk about it.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Brian Windhorst on Bob Iger's post-Disney career
quotes.excerpt: When he retired from Disney the first time he worked at Thrive Capital.
quotes.quote: When he retired from Disney the first time he worked at Thrive Capital. He was an advisor there, they were doing deals. And then when he retired from Disney for good, I guess the the second time, he became very involved in what is the new fund, Thrive Eternal, which is this fund that's now involved in the sports franchises, which is supposed to kind of value iconic brands. That's what they pitched this fund as.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Brian Windhorst on Bob Iger's Knicks fandom
quotes.excerpt: I got to know him because he would sit center court at Clipper games.
quotes.quote: I got to know him because he would sit center court at Clipper games. And we just would go up and talk to him. He was a big fan, that's how he got to be friends with Chris Paul and Chris kind of sought him out as a mentor. They've developed a genuine friendship and mentorship over the years. But Bob also tried to bring the NFL to Los Angeles about a decade ago. He was involved in a project down in Carson, it was going to be the Chargers and the Raiders down there. They kind of got outmaneuvered by your guy Jerry Jones and Stan Kroenke and then they built the the the Rams and Chargers ended up building SoFi Stadium, which is this jewel of a stadium now in Los Angeles.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Brian Windhorst on Jeff Schwartz's statement
quotes.excerpt: A statement from Excel Basketball. Now Jeff Schwartz is one of the top three.
quotes.quote: A statement from Excel Basketball. Now Jeff Schwartz is one of the top three. I don't want to get into all this stuff, CAA, Rich Paul, WME, whatever. He's one of the top agents in all of sports. He has, his company is worth billions of dollars because it does all kinds of other deals. Excel is his company, it makes a statement from Jeff Schwartz. I want to tell you, Jeff Schwartz is almost never quoted, ever. He is an extremely powerful, extremely distinguished, extremely respected guy who moves through his actions, not his words, and doesn't seek the spotlight, is, you know, a power broker, old school style.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Brian Windhorst on Jeff Schwartz's tweet
quotes.excerpt: Incredible, the Lakers sell for 12B, yet teams won't spend on older vets because of current CBA rules.
quotes.quote: Incredible, the Lakers sell for 12B, yet teams won't spend on older vets because of current CBA rules. Thank you, Union.
